notes: Same access route/method as bs168 (direct HTTP, no block). Full catalog-tree search (see bs168 notes) found breadcrumb 'Sale' (/c/sale-7) > 'Clearance & Outlet' (/c/sale-7/clearance-outlet-15029) with 8 direct children: 'All Clearance' plus 7 department splits (Furniture/Outdoor/Tabletop & Bar/Kitchen/Decor/Rugs/Bed & Bath Clearance). The explicit on-site wording 'Clearance & Outlet' (not a generic 'Sale' label) satisfies the Clearance-vs-Sale test directly - no ambiguity flag needed. EXCLUDED as generic temporary promotion (Sale-vs-Clearance test): 'All Sale' (/c/sale-7/shop-all-sale), the sibling of Clearance & Outlet under the 'Sale' parent - generically named, no clearance/outlet/permanent-markdown signal. DEDUP CHECK on 'Clearance & Outlet' vs its own child 'All Clearance': the parent's own direct-category API query returns totalResults=1582 vs the child 'All Clearance' query returning 1578 - very close but not identical. Compared actual product-code sets (not just counts, per project convention): fetched both listings sorted name-asc, pageSize=300, and the first 300 product codes were 100% identical between the two (0 codes unique to either side in that sample) - strong evidence 'Clearance & Outlet' is functionally the same 'everything' view as 'All Clearance', with the parent's own aggregate query picking up ~4 extra subtree-only items 'All Clearance' doesn't separately list. To avoid reporting two near-duplicate 'everything' counts, 'Clearance & Outlet' is kept as the structural is_group parent (matching the site's own taxonomy) with no qty of its own, and 'All Clearance' is kept as the qty-bearing leaf for 'all clearance items', alongside the 7 genuine department sub-listings (Rule: compare product-ID sets not names, same method the prior Home-Decor pass used on this platform). Department qtys do not sum to All Clearance's 1578 (they sum to 913) - expected, since many clearance SKUs are not assigned to any of the 7 named departments and only appear in the 'All Clearance' catch-all, not an error.
